title: EPS-95 pensioners and the higher pension question
author: Editorial Desk
summary: Millions of retired private sector employees live on a small monthly pension. What they ask for.
body:
The **Employees' Pension Scheme, 1995 (EPS-95)** is run by the EPFO and pays a monthly pension to retired workers of the organised sector who have contributed for at least ten years.

## The issue

Many pensioners receive a **minimum pension** of ₹1,000 a month, a figure that has not been revised for years. Pensioners' organisations have asked for a substantial increase, with a minimum that reflects the cost of living, along with dearness allowance and medical benefits.

## The higher pension case

In November 2022, the Supreme Court upheld the provision allowing eligible employees to contribute on actual salary above the wage ceiling to get a **higher pension**, and set conditions and timelines. The EPFO set up a process for applications, and many applicants have faced delays and queries.

## BMS and pensioners

BMS has a federation of senior citizens, the **Varisht Nagarik Parisangh**, and has joined representations on the minimum pension. It has also asked the EPFO to simplify and speed up the higher pension process.

## Why it matters

Pension is deferred wage. For a worker who has served for decades, a very small pension is a broken promise, and a society is judged by how it treats those who have retired.
